topic: Build-readiness review of the eleven planned phases of packet specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build (001-activity-and-actor, 002-routine-layer, 003-terminal-screen, 004-computer-exposure, 005-memory, 006-approval-grants, 007-per-bot-apps, 008-vault, 009-skills, 010-conversations, 011-messaging-channels). Each phase has spec.md, plan.md, tasks.md and acceptance-criteria.md. They were written in parallel, each alone, and nobody has checked them against the built runtime or against each other. This is a review of plans, not new design research. Evidence (read-only): the phase docs; the built skilled-bots runtime (.skilled/skills/system-skilled-bots/runtime/lib/, .skilled/bin/bots.cjs, .skilled/skills/system-skilled-bots/scripts/bot-check.cjs, runtime/tests/); the parity research synthesis specs/system-skilled-bots/002-openbot-parity-research/research/research.md; the reference repos under specs/system-skilled-bots/context/ (OpenBot-main, OpenMausBot-main, rakazo-main, openhuman-main, OpenGhost-main, hermes-muse-main, turnstone-main, buzz-main, tinychannels-main). Four angles: 1. Plan versus runtime: do the files, functions, records, fields and verbs each plan names exist with the shapes it assumes, and are its test and verify commands runnable here? 2. Cross-phase consistency: do the phases agree on shared records (by: actor, grants, operators.json, conversation JSONL, memory files, state-root layout, HonoredPosture fields, bots --json output read by the terminal screen and the channels), and are the build order and dependencies sound? 3. Parity gaps and overbuild: for a small team, what is still missing after all eleven phases, and what do the plans build that is not needed or duplicates another phase or the runtime? 4. Security and failure modes: secret leakage, token storage, spoofed chat users, who may approve, restarts, lost or duplicated messages and answers, concurrent approvals from terminal and chat, prompt injection through memory, skills or chat, routine until and fatigue edge cases. Every finding names the phase, the doc and line, the evidence with [SOURCE: path:line], a severity (P0 blocks the build, P1 wrong or missing, P2 polish) and the exact spec edit that fixes it. End with findings grouped by phase and ranked, plus a cross-phase conflict list.

focus: Angle 4's security half — secret leakage paths, token storage, spoofed chat users and who may approve, tested against the runtime's record shape, the vault's storage claim and the channel link's identity model.
keyQuestions: Security and failure modes: secret leakage, token storage, spoofed chat users, who may approve, and the other named failure classes.

focus: The --json payloads the terminal and the channels consume: does each producer promise the keys its consumer parses?
keyQuestions: Plan versus runtime: do the files, functions, records, fields and verbs each plan names exist with the shapes it assumes?
noveltyJustification: All three findings are new: the seven-group versus six-marker mismatch with no per-row status field, the routines JSON missing botId, and the inbox JSON naming fields in prose rather than exact keys.

focus: Angle 2's remaining half — each phase declares a handoff that the next phase depends on; does every handoff name an observable state the next phase's setup step can test, and does any handoff claim a dependency that does not exist or contradict the phase's own change?
keyQuestions: Cross-phase consistency: do the phases agree on shared records and are the build order and dependencies sound?
noveltyJustification: Two findings are new (the false 008-to-009 dependency and the five-value rung enum against a four-rung doc), and the index handoff is a partially new consequence of the known schema conflict, now failing the phase's own exit criterion.

focus: The closure layer: every requirement has an acceptance row, no acceptance row cites a missing requirement, and every [P0] checklist row names a check that can run.
keyQuestions: Plan versus runtime: are each phase's test and verify commands runnable here?
noveltyJustification: All three findings are new: four command-less P0 rows in phase 011, the CHK-002 label/command mismatch in 002 and 009, and phase 008's Met-count gate that rejects a waiver.
sourcesQueried: all eleven REQ and AC tables (mechanical diff)

focus: The run folder and the child environment — phase 008 promises a stored value never reaches the prompt, the run folder, the run record or a delivery message; this pass tested the run-folder sink against what the runner writes.
keyQuestions: Security and failure modes: secret leakage, token storage, spoofed chat users, who may approve, and the other named failure classes.
noveltyJustification: The single finding is new: the child stdout capture at runFolder/stdout.log makes the never-the-run-folder promise unenforceable, and no earlier iteration read the run folder's own files.

focus: Consolidation — duplicate check, fix order, and the parent-level edits that settle more than one finding.
keyQuestions: Cross-phase consistency: do the phases agree on shared records and are the build order and dependencies sound?
